title: Head of AI Automation
description:
About Dispensed

At Dispensed ,we are passionate about empowering individuals to reach their full potential by supporting better health outcomes. We believe that access to innovative and alternative therapies can transform lives. Through our telehealth platform, we facilitate patient access to affordable, efficient, and reliable alternative medicine services across Australia, NZ and the UK.

About the role

Across the business, our teams are doing manual work every day that a well-built system could take on instead. We want one person whose job is to find that work and give teams their time back by building real automation and putting it into production.

We're a telehealth business operating across Australia, the UK and New Zealand, covering patient onboarding, prescriber workflows, pharmacy fulfilment, clinical admin and patient support. We've already proven this kind of work can be automated - now we want to build it in-house.

This is a hands-on role - less overseeing, more building and delivering.

What you'll own

• Work alongside teams to identify the parts of their work that could be automated

• Build the automation, agent, tool or integration that fixes it, and get it into production

• Measure the impact - establish a baseline before you start, then track what changed

• Set the team up for success by handing over automations once they're stable, documented and the team knows how to run it

• Keep track of what's newly possible in AI and turn that into things we can stop doing manually

• Bring the AI enablement work we currently outsource in-house

Your first 90 days will focus on three areas: patient support, then clinic and prescriber operations, then pharmacy order operations. Ideally, you'll have something built and running within a month.

What you'll need

Essential:

• Proven experience building AI-powered agents, apps, automations or internal tools that saw real use

• The ability to code and deploy independently, without relying on other teams

• Solid skills in prompting, evaluation, retrieval, APIs, and data handling, plus enough security awareness to handle patient data properly

• A good instinct for finding where the real time savings are in an unfamiliar process

• The ability to earn trust with busy, non-technical operators

• Able to work without a ready-made backlog - you identify what needs doing

Nice to have:

• Experience in healthcare, telehealth or another regulated industry

• Background in forward-deployed or solutions engineering

• Founder or early-stage startup experience

Things to know before applying:

• We operate under Australian privacy law, UK GDPR and NZ requirements, plus medicinal cannabis regulation in three countries. Some automations need a different approach

• Success means what's still running six months later, not how many things were built

• This role works best when it fits naturally into how teams already operate

What We Offer

• Work From Anywhere

• A competitive salary & benefits package

• A supportive and positive work environment

How to apply

Send us your CV plus a couple of examples of what you've built - an agent, a tool, an automation. A repo, video or a short write-up. Applications without a build example won't be considered.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Anduril Imaging team develops state-of-the-art imaging systems across both hardware and software, deployed to tackle the most significant security challenges of America and its allies. The team is heavily involved in utilizing computer vision, perception, electro-optical, infrared, and sensor data to give the US and its allies an advantage. We are extending that capability into orbit - building space-based EO/IR and sensing payloads under a New Space philosophy: aggressive schedules, commercial-cadence engineering, and a relentless bias toward flying hardware. Our standard is to take a payload from architecture to orbit in a year or less, not the multi-year timelines that have traditionally defined space programs.

ABOUT THE JOB

As an Electronics Designer on the Anduril Imaging team, you will own the electronics architecture for space-bound imaging payloads and drive their design from concept through flight. This is a system-level role for an engineer who can hold the whole payload in their head - defining the electrical architecture, making the build-versus-buy and COTS-versus-rad-hard tradeoffs that keep schedule and cost in check, and then going hands-on to lay out, bring up, and qualify the hardware. You will set the technical direction for power, sensor, and interface electronics, and remain hands-on to see your individual designs take flight. You will work in rapid design cycles where the goal is to get capable, robust hardware into space in twelve months or less. You will make well-informed engineering judgments about which requirements are load-bearing and which aren't, iterate on real hardware, and demonstrate the discipline to design for manufacturability, test, and EMI/EMC compliance from day one. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy and be a technical anchor for less experienced engineers on the team.

• Own the electrical architecture for imaging payloads, partitioning the system, defining power, sensor, data, and interface electronics, and driving the architectural tradeoffs (COTS vs. rad-hard, performance vs. schedule vs. cost) that enable a rapid path to orbit.

• Lead the design, layout, bring-up, and qualification of PCBAs spanning analog, mixed-signal, FPGAs, and power electronics for EO/IR sensor systems.

• Translate sensor and system performance models into electrical requirements, and push back on requirements that don't earn their place on the critical path.

• Drive rapid design-build-test cycles: prototype quickly, characterize on the bench, iterate on real hardware, and converge on flight-ready designs without unnecessary cycles.

• Design for the space environment (radiation, thermal extremes, vacuum, vibration, and launch loads) and own the analysis and testing (TVAC, vibe, EMI/EMC) that proves it.

• Bake in design for manufacturability and assembly (DFM/DFA) from the first schematic so designs scale cleanly toward low-rate production as programs mature.

• Lead board bring-up, integration, and troubleshooting in the lab and during environmental and integration testing, using standard bench equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, DMMs, etc.).
